newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen dry until Wednesday, then rainy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen dry until Wednesday, then rainy.

text.p: The U.S. Midwest should be warm and dry until Wednesday but rain and colder weather was expected across most of the Corn Belt Thursday and Friday, meteorologists said.

"We're going to go from a warm, dry pattern early this week to a cool, damp, possibly wet pattern," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express. "There is a possibility of four or five days of what looks like a lot more moisture than we've had in the Corn Belt."
Gesser forecast rainfall amounts of mostly less than 0.75 inch with 60 to 70 percent coverage later this week.
Temperatures were expected to peak in the 40s and 50s degrees Farenheit, he said.
Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said rainfall amounts would range from 0.50 to 1.50 inches with general coverage in the northern corn belt.
Coverage in southwest Illinois and and the southwest Corn Belt was expected to be 60 percent, he said.
"It looks like we'll have some rain or showers throughout most of the Midwest Thursday and Friday," Burgio said.
Temperatures will likely be four to eight degrees below normal by Saturday, Burgio said.
Gesser said clouds would linger across the western corn belt on Sunday and in the east on Monday.
Long-range forecasts indicated a warm-up early next week, he said.
